subject: Post-call recap: GlobalMed private VPC / on-prem discovery
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@globalmed.com>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@globalmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: GlobalMed private VPC / on-prem discovery

Hi Sanjay / Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. If I missed anything, please flag.

Summary of needs / drivers:
- Regulatory: GlobalMed needs PHI to remain in a customer-managed VPC or on-prem environment for HIPAA compliance and internal auditability.
- Air-gap option: some sites will require an air-gapped on-prem deployment for certain workloads (research lab), while others are ok with VPC peers to a central environment.
- Networking constraints: strict egress controls, only specific outbound endpoints allowed, and traffic must traverse GlobalMed-managed transit gateway.
- Data residency: production inference must remain in US regions and be isolated per business unit.
- SLA/availability: primary requirement is predictable latency for triage workflows; throughput peaks during business hours.

Primary goals:
1) Proof-of-concept: deploy a private instance (VPC peered) to validate latency and KV cache behavior with representative workloads.
2) Security review: provide SOC2 summary, network diagram, and KMS integration notes.
3) Delivery plan: outline timelines and a mutually agreed MxP (mutual action plan) for the POC -> pilot -> production path.

Open / confirmed constraints we captured:
- GlobalMed will not permit direct outbound internet from inference hosts except to a controlled egress proxy.
- KMS must be customer-managed with support for AWS KMS / external HSM integration.
- We need to validate whether the research lab air-gapped site can accept a signed appliance image or if a full on-prem install is required.

Attachments shared: globalmed-network-requirements.pdf (from your network team), Redwood SOC2 summary (attached).

Next steps (owners & timing):
- Redwood to share: preliminary network diagram + list of required CIDR ranges and egress endpoints (Camila) — by EOD Thu (2027-06-17).
- Redwood to schedule technical deep-dive with Vivek and GlobalMed infra (Sanjay) — propose Fri (2027-06-18) morning PT.
- GlobalMed to confirm: list of air-gapped sites and security contact for appliance transfer (Sanjay) — by Mon (2027-06-21).

If that looks right, I’ll create a short MxP and HubSpot record with milestones and owners.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Cc: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@globalmed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: GlobalMed private VPC / on-prem discovery

Camila — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed: PHI cannot leave our VPC for processing; VPC peering or private link-style connectivity is required.
- Egress: we only allow outbound to a small set of IPs via our egress proxy; we will provide the ACL list to your network team.
- KMS: AWS KMS is preferred; we can evaluate HSM later for the air-gapped site.
- Air-gap sites: three sites may require air-gapped installs (Lab-A, Lab-B, Lab-C). We need a path that allows offline package transfer + signed artifact verification.

Questions for Redwood:
1) What is your recommended approach for the air-gapped install? Appliance image vs. install script? Any bandwidth/size constraints for transferring model artifacts?
2) For the POC, can you support a single-tenant deployment in our shared VPC with strict host-level egress controls?

We’re good to do the technical deep-dive on Fri morning PT — suggest 8:30am PT. I’ll invite our infra lead (Elena) and our security manager if available.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Director, Platform Engineering | GlobalMed Healthcare
sanjay.rao@globalmed.com | +1 (617) 555-0890

Hi Sanjay — appreciate the fast responses. Answers inline below and next steps updated: 

- Air-gapped installs: we support both appliance-style signed images (recommended for fully air-gapped sites) and a scripted on-prem installer. Appliance images are ~3.5GB compressed for the runtime layer; model artifacts vary — we typically stream models during initial sync and can provide a tarball for offline transfer if needed. We’ll confirm specific model sizes once we lock the model family for POC.
- Single-tenant in shared VPC: yes — we can run a customer-dedicated tenant in your VPC with host-level egress constrained to your proxy endpoints. We’ll provide the exact CIDR/IPs and domains that need to be allowed.

Updated next steps / owners:
- Camila: share preliminary network diagram + required endpoints (EOD Thu 2027-06-17).
- Vivek: prepare POC deployment runbook (appliance vs installer options) and model artifact sizing by Thu (Vivek).
- GlobalMed: confirm air-gapped sites and security contact (Sanjay) — Mon 2027-06-21.

I’ll send a calendar hold for Fri 8:30am PT and include a technical agenda. Looking forward to the dive.

Best,
Camila

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@globalmed.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: GlobalMed private VPC / on-prem discovery

Morning team — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

1) Appliance vs installer trade-offs:
- Appliance (signed VM image): fastest for locked-down sites; smaller operational surface but requires secure transfer process and verification.
- Installer (scripted): more flexible for heterogeneous infra but requires outbound access during install for dependencies unless you bundle them.

2) Model artifact sizes: for POC we recommend a distilled model variant (~6-8GB) to keep transfer times reasonable; full production model families can be 30GB+. If you want, we can pre-package the POC model into a compressed tarball and checksum for offline transfer.

3) Network endpoints: Redwood runtime will need to reach our control plane for health checks and licensing if you opt for the VPC peered deployment. If air-gapped, we can set a short-lived license token and an offline validation flow. Expect a list of ~12 endpoints (control, telemetry, updates). We’ll put exact IPs/CIDRs in the diagram Camila is sending.

I’ll attach a short runbook stub to the calendar invite. See you Fri.

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
